title: Display Colour Filter – Colour filters for each display on your Mac
description: A free menu bar app for Mac that turns colour filters such as greyscale on or off for each display separately.
lead: macOS can turn your screen greyscale or apply a colour filter, but only to every display at once. Display Colour Filter is a small menu bar app that lets you decide, display by display, whether a filter is on and which one. For example, you can keep an external monitor in greyscale to cut down on distraction while your Mac’s built-in display stays in full colour.
features: Turn the filter on or off for each display
Choose a filter for each display: Greyscale, Red/Green, Green/Red, Blue/Yellow or Colour Tint
Adjust the intensity (and the hue for Colour Tint), using the same filters as macOS
Remembers the settings for each display, and can open automatically at login
In English, Japanese, Chinese, Korean, French, German and Spanish
installSteps: Open the disk image and drag DisplayColourFilter to Applications.
gatekeeper: The app is free and open source, but it isn’t notarised by Apple, so macOS blocks it the first time you open it. To open it anyway:
gatekeeperSteps: When macOS says the app can’t be opened, click Done.
Open System Settings › Privacy & Security, scroll down and click Open Anyway next to the message about DisplayColourFilter.
Confirm with your password or Touch ID, then click Open Anyway once more.
gatekeeperNote: You only need to do this once.
usage: Click the icon in the menu bar and switch on the filter for the display you want. Choose the filter and adjust the intensity – changes take effect immediately. The gear menu at the bottom right has Open at Login, Check for Updates… and Quit.
notes: Keep the system’s own colour filter (System Settings › Accessibility › Display › Colour filters) turned off while you use the app.
Filters work on displays connected directly to your Mac: built-in, USB‑C, Thunderbolt and HDMI. They have no effect on DisplayLink, AirPlay or Sidecar displays.
When you quit the app, every display goes back to the system setting.
disclaimer: Display Colour Filter is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple Inc.
